rules.title: Good cause required for non-renewal of leases
rules.requirement: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.summary_plain: In New Jersey, landlords generally must have good cause to refuse to renew a lease, except for certain small owner-occupied buildings and transient units.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, los propietarios generalmente deben tener una causa justificada para negarse a renovar un contrato de arrendamiento, excepto en ciertos edificios pequeños ocupados por el propietario y unidades transitorias.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all residential rental properties except owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units.
rules.exemptions_text: Owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

rules.title: Eviction for continuing nuisance caused by pet
rules.requirement: A landlord may require a tenant to remove a pet if the pet is a continuing nuisance to the welfare or property of the landlord or other residents and may file for eviction if the tenant does not remove the pet.
rules.summary_plain: If a pet causes ongoing problems affecting others or the property, the landlord can require its removal and evict the tenant if necessary.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si una mascota causa problemas continuos que afectan a otros o a la propiedad, el propietario puede exigir su remoción y desalojar al inquilino si es necesario.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all rental housing where pets are kept.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may require a tenant to remove a pet from the rental premises if the pet is a continuing nuisance to the welfare or property of the landlord or the other residents. If the tenant does not remove the pet, the landlord may file for an eviction action for violating the lease due to a continuing nuisance created by the pet.

rules.title: Lease termination for disabling illness, accident, or death
rules.requirement: A tenant may terminate a lease early with 40 days written notice if suffering a disabling illness, accident, or death of tenant or spouse, under certain conditions.
rules.summary_plain: Tenants in New Jersey can break their lease early for disabling illness, accident, or death by giving 40 days written notice and meeting certain conditions.
rules.summary_plain_es: Los inquilinos en Nueva Jersey pueden romper su contrato de arrendamiento anticipadamente por enfermedad discapacitante, accidente o muerte, dando un aviso escrito de 40 días y cumpliendo ciertas condiciones.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants with disabling illness, accident, or death of tenant or spouse.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply if lease specifically provides otherwise.
rules.quoted_span: A tenant may terminate a lease for the following reasons: ... Lease Termination Due to Disabling Illness, Accident or Death Law, a tenant may break their lease, under certain conditions. A 40-day written notice of lease termination is required in each instance.
